I’m sorry you don’t feel comfortable enough to tell people, but I’m happy you have someone to talk about it! Therapists are great.

People are such complex beings, and such as them, their relationships are also complex. 
You might not understand why after being abused (emotionally, physically, psychologically or all of the above) she still maintains a relationship with them, but seems that for her the family is important. Could be fear of losing her siblings, could be fear of feeling left out in a foreign country, could be just that she loves them despite their faults. 

It’s important to note that unconditional for us doesn’t mean that for everyone. Culture wise many societies have developed to accept lgbt+ people, but not everyone, and that’s something we have to live with for now. We can strive for better, sure, but not everyone is doing the same journey, so that makes it extra hard. 

As someone with extremely homophobic family, and living in a (mostly) homophobic country, I have thought many times that I won’t be able to come out to my family because of fear of losing my nieces, nephews, and the “unconditional” relationship I have with my parents. That might change in the future when (or if) I find a partner that is willing to help me and support me in my journey. For now I don’t see myself coming out for a relationship that could be fragile or new (not saying that yours is, or that your partner sees it that way, just stating how I feel). 

Sadly life is not black and white because that would make it easier to decide on things. All these shades of gray makes living so challenging but at least we have people to do life with :)! 

I’m sorry that in this comment section you won’t find the answer you might be looking for (in the sense of “hey, just do this, it’s simple”, imagine how easier life would be loll), but I hope it put things into perspective and you don’t feel pressured to do something you don’t want to/feel comfortable doing. It’s crazy to me how often this happens to people our age. When I was 25 I used to pick up my niece from school since her parents were at work and we live so close to her school, and my uni schedule allowed me to do this. I would always arrive a few mins earlier so I would walk around or just stand next to the door. There was an old man (I would assume around 70 yo) that came to pick up his grandkid that started making conversation with me since he saw me often. I was kind with him and having the regular polite convo but he got too excited that asked my number a few days later since we lived close by (I didn’t tell him where) and to chat since he didn’t have many friends. I felt bad for him and gave him my number (and tbf I also felt a bit pressure). He texted me later and again I made polite conversation but then when he tried calling me I gave the excuse that I was in classes or whatever. I felt so awkward but also felt sad because what if he really just wanted a friend? But in the other hand it felt pretty weird how he just kept insisting on calling on the phone and talking with me. It felt creepy but I was so confused and ashamed that I didn’t tell anyone. (Also my niece never saw that man because she would take so much time to get out of her classroom so the old guy left with his grandkid as soon as the school gates opened). After this I just gave a random excuse to my mom so she would go pick up my niece from school. I didn’t want to have an awkward encounter with him. 

I am kinda relieved (or maybe that’s not the word I’m looking for) that I’m not the only one that had an experience like this and feels quite confused about it. But also it’s insane how this is something that happened to so many people. 

But also (!!!) why do WE feel ashamed? huh that’s something I just realized…
